title: Remark
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(1)]
  \item When the group $\pi=\{1\}$, we could recover the notion of Hopf braces.
  \item In any Hopf $\pi$-brace, $1_\circ=1$. Indeed, setting $g=h=1_\circ$ in \eqref{eq:Hbrace} one obtains $1_\circ \ell=\ell$ for all $\ell\in H_\gamma$. Similarly, $g=\ell=1_\circ$ yields $h1_\circ=h$ for all $h\in H_\beta$.
  \item  $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ is called cocommutative if $H_\alpha$ is cocommutative for each $\alpha\in\pi$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Example
body_md:
Let $(H,\cdot,\circ,S,T)$ be a Hopf brace and $\pi=Aut(H)$ the group of automorphisms of Hopf brace $H$. For each $\alpha\in\pi$, $H_\alpha=H$ as a vector space. We denote the element in $H_\alpha$ by $h^\alpha=\alpha(h)$ for $h\in H$. Define
\begin{align*}
&\cdot_{\alpha,\beta}:H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta\rightarrow H_{\alpha\beta},\ g^\alpha\otimes h^\beta\mapsto (g \cdot h)^{\alpha\beta},\\
&\circ_{\alpha,\beta}:H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta\rightarrow H_{\alpha\beta},\ g^\alpha\otimes h^\beta\mapsto (g \circ h)^{\alpha\beta},\\
&1_\cdot=1_\circ=1,\quad \Delta_\alpha=\Delta,\quad \varepsilon_\alpha=\varepsilon,\\
&S_\alpha:H_\alpha\rightarrow H_{\bar{\alpha}},\ h^\alpha\mapsto S(h)^{\bar{\alpha}},\\
&T_\alpha:H_\alpha\rightarrow H_{\bar{\alpha}},\ h^\alpha\mapsto T(h)^{\bar{\alpha}}.
\end{align*}
Denote $\cdot=\{\cdot_{\alpha,\beta}\}_{\alpha,\beta\in\pi},\circ=\{\circ_{\alpha,\beta}\}_{\alpha,\beta\in\pi},S=\{S_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi},T=\{T_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi})$, then $(H,\cdot,S,\circ,T$ is a Hopf $\pi$-brace.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $H=\{H_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ be a Hopf $\pi$-algebra, and $K$ a Hopf algebra. Then $H$ is called a {\bf left $K$-$\pi$-module} with the action $\rightharpoondown=\{\rightharpoondown_\alpha: K\otimes H_\alpha \rightarrow H_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ 
if every $H_\alpha$ is a $H$-module. And $H$ is called a {\bf left $K$-$\pi$-module $\pi$-bialgebra} if the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[\quad\rm(1)]
  \item $k\rightharpoondown_{\alpha\beta}(hg)=(k_{(1)}\rightharpoondown_{\alpha}h)(k_{(2)}\rightharpoondown_{\beta}h)$,
  \item $k\rightharpoondown_{e}1_e=\varepsilon_K(k)1_e$,
  \item $(k\rightharpoondown_{\alpha}h)_{(1,\alpha)} \otimes (k\rightharpoondown_{\alpha}h)_{(2,\alpha)} = (k_{(1)}\rightharpoondown_{\alpha}h_{(1,\alpha)})\otimes(k_{(2)}\rightharpoondown_{\alpha}h_{(2,\alpha)})$,
  \item $\varepsilon_\alpha(k\rightharpoondown_\alpha h)=\varepsilon_K(k)\varepsilon_\alpha(h)$.
\end{enumerate}
for all $h\in H_\alpha, g\in H_\beta, \alpha,\beta\in\pi$, $k\in K$.

title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:pimod}
Let $H=\{H_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ be a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra, $K$ a cocommutative Hopf algebra, 
and $H$ a left $K$-module  $\pi$-bialgebra as above. 
Then the smash product $(H\sharp K=\{H_\alpha\sharp K\}_{\alpha\in\pi},\cdot,\circ)$ is a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-brace with the following structures:
\begin{eqnarray*}
  (h\sharp k)\cdot_{\alpha\beta}(h'\sharp k') &=& hh'\sharp kk', \\
  (h\sharp k)\circ_{\alpha\beta}(h'\sharp k') &=& h(k_{(1)}\rightharpoondown_{\beta}h')\sharp k_{(2)}k', \\
  S_{H_\alpha\sharp K}(h\sharp k) &=& S_\alpha(h)\sharp S_K(k), \\
  T_{H_\alpha\sharp K}(h\sharp k) &=& S_K(k_{(1)})\rightharpoondown_{\bar{\alpha}}S_\alpha(h)\sharp S_K(k_{(2)}), 
\end{eqnarray*}
for all $h\in H_\alpha, h'\in H_\beta, \alpha,\beta\in\pi$, $k,k'\in K$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Equation~\eqref{eq:Hbrace} implies that
\begin{equation*}	                 
\varepsilon_\beta(h)g = g\circ (h_{(1,\beta)}S_{\beta}(h_{(2,\beta)})) = (g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)})S_{\alpha}(g_{(2,\alpha)})(g_{(3,\alpha)}\circ S_{\beta}(h_{(2,\beta)}))
\end{equation*}
holds for all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta,~ \alpha,\beta\in\pi$, and hence,
\begin{align*}
S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h)g_{(2,\alpha)} &= S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)}\varepsilon_\beta(h_{(2,\beta)}))g_{(2,\alpha)} \\
&= S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)})\varepsilon_\beta(h_{(2,\beta)})g_{(2,\alpha)}\\
&=S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)})(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ h_{(2,\beta)})S_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})(g_{(4,\alpha)}\circ S_\beta(h_{(3,\beta)}))\\
&=\varepsilon_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)})S_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})(g_{(3,\alpha)}\circ S_\beta(h_{(2,\beta)}))\\
&=S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)})(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ S_\beta(h)).
\end{align*}
This completes the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
(1)For $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta,\ell\in H_\gamma$, it is clear that, $1\rightharpoonup_\alpha h=S_e(1)(1\circ h)=h$ and 
$$g\rightharpoonup_\alpha 1=S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)})(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ 1)=S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)})g_{(2,\alpha)}=\varepsilon_\alpha(g)1.$$

And
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & g \rightharpoonup_\alpha (h\rightharpoonup_\beta\ell )\\
&=& S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)}) (g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ (S_\beta(h_{(1,\beta)})(h_{(2,\beta)}\circ \ell ))) \\
&\overset{(\ref{eq:Hbrace})}{=}& S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)}) (g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ S_\beta(h_{(1,\beta)})) S_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}) (g_{(4,\alpha)}\circ h_{(2,\beta)}\circ \ell ) \\
&\overset{(\ref{eq:Hbrace2})}{=}& S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)}) g_{(2,\alpha)} S_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}) (g_{(4,\alpha)}\circ h_{(2,\beta)}\circ \ell ) \\
&=& S_{\alpha}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h_{(1,\beta)}) ((g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ h_{(2,\beta)})\circ \ell ) \\
&=& (g\circ h)\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta} \ell ,
\end{eqnarray*}
and
\begin{eqnarray*}
g\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}(hk) &=& S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)}) (g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ(hk)) \\
 &=& S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)}) (g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ h)S_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}) (g_{(4,\alpha)}\circ k)\\
 &=& (g_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha h)(g_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha k).
\end{eqnarray*}
Therefore, $H$ is a left $H_{\circ}$-$\pi$-module $\pi$-algebra.

(2) For all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
 g_{(1,\alpha)}(g_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha h) 
 &=& g_{(1,\alpha)}S_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})(g_{(3,\alpha)}\circ h) \\
 &=& \varepsilon_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)})(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ h) = g\circ h,
\end{eqnarray*}
and
\begin{eqnarray*}
 g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(T_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}} h) 
 &=& g_{(1,\alpha)}(g_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha(T_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha} h)) \\
 &=& g_{(1,\alpha)}((g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ T_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)}))\rightharpoonup_{e} h) \\
 &=& g_{(1,\alpha)}\varepsilon_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})(1\rightharpoonup_{e} h) = gh.
\end{eqnarray*}

(3) If $H$ is cocommutative, it is straightforward to verify that $H$ is a left $H_{\circ}$-$\pi$-module like $\pi$-bialgebra.
For all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
S_\beta(g\rightharpoonup_\alpha h) &=& S_\beta(S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)})(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ h)) \\
 &=& S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h)S_{\bar{\alpha}}S_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})\\
 &=& S_{\alpha\beta}(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ h)g_{(2,\alpha)} \\
 &=& S_\alpha(g_{(1,\alpha)})(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ S_\beta(h)) \\
 &=& g\rightharpoonup_{\alpha} S_\beta(h). 
\end{eqnarray*}
These finish the proof.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $\pi$ be an abelian group and $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-brace, then each $H_\alpha$ is a right $H_\circ$-$\pi$-module like coalgebra under the action
$$a\leftharpoonup_\beta x=T_\beta(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)})\circ a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)},$$
for all $a\in H_\alpha,x\in H_\beta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For all $a\in H_\alpha,x\in H_\beta,y\in H_\gamma$,
\begin{align*}
&(a\leftharpoonup_\beta x)\leftharpoonup_\gamma y\\
&=(T_\beta(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)})\circ a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)})\leftharpoonup_\gamma y\\
&=T_{\bar{\gamma}}((T_\beta(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)})\circ a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup y_{(1,\gamma)})\circ T_\beta(a_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(3,\beta)})\circ a_{(4,\alpha)}\circ x_{(4,\beta)}\circ y_{(2,\gamma)}\\
&=T_{\beta\gamma}((a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)})\circ(T_\beta(a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta}  ((a_{(3,\alpha)}\circ x_{(3,\beta)})\rightharpoonup y_{(1,\gamma)})))\circ a_{(4,\alpha)}\circ x_{(4,\beta)}\circ y_{(2,\gamma)}\\
&=T_{\beta\gamma}((a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)}) ((a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta} y_{(1,\gamma)})))\circ a_{(3,\alpha)}\circ x_{(3,\beta)}\circ y_{(2,\gamma)}\\
&=T_{\beta\gamma}(S_\alpha(a_{(1,\alpha)})(a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(1,\beta)})S_{\alpha\beta}(a_{(3,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)})(a_{(4,\alpha)}\circ x_{(3,\beta)}\circ y_{(1,\gamma)}))\circ a_{(5,\alpha)}\circ x_{(4,\beta)}\circ y_{(2,\gamma)}\\
&=T_{\beta\gamma}(S_\alpha(a_{(1,\alpha)})(a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(1,\beta)}\circ y_{(1,\gamma)}))\circ a_{(3,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)}\circ y_{(2,\gamma)}\\
&=T_{\beta\gamma}(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha(x_{(1,\beta)}\circ y_{(1,\gamma)}))\circ a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)}\circ y_{(2,\gamma)}\\
&=a\leftharpoonup_{\beta\gamma} (x\circ y),
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align*}
&\Delta_\alpha(a\leftharpoonup_\beta x)=\Delta_\alpha(T_\beta(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)})\circ a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)})\\
&=T_\beta(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(1,\beta)})\circ a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ x_{(2,\beta)}\otimes T_\beta(a_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha x_{(3,\beta)})\circ a_{(4,\alpha)}\circ x_{(4,\beta)}\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta x_{(1,\beta)}\otimes a_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta x_{(2,\beta)}.
\end{align*}
The proof is completed.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $\pi$ be an abelian group and $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-brace. Define $c_{\alpha,\beta}:H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta\rightarrow H_\beta\otimes H_\alpha$ by
$$c_{\alpha,\beta}(x\otimes y)=x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha y_{(1,\beta)}\otimes x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta y_{(2,\beta)},\ \forall x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta,$$
and $\sigma_{\alpha,\beta}:H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta\rightarrow H_\beta\otimes H_\alpha$ by
$$\sigma_{\alpha,\beta}(x\otimes y)=y_{(1,\alpha)}\otimes S_\beta(y_{(2,\beta)})ay_{(3,\alpha)},$$
then $c=\{c_{\alpha,\beta}\}$ and $\sigma=\{\sigma_{\alpha,\beta}\}$ produce isomorphic representations of the braid group $B_n$ on $H_{\alpha_1}\otimes H_{\alpha_2}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\alpha_n}$ for $n\geq2$ and $\alpha_i\in\pi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Define $f_n,g_n:H_{\alpha_1}\otimes H_{\alpha_2}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\alpha_n}\rightarrow H_{\alpha_1}\otimes H_{\alpha_2}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\alpha_n}$ as follows
$$g_n(a^{\alpha_1}\otimes a^{\alpha_2}\otimes\cdots\otimes a^{\alpha_n})=a^{\alpha_1}_{(1,\alpha_1)}\otimes a^{\alpha_1}_{(2,\alpha_1)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha_1}a^{\alpha_2}\otimes\cdots\otimes a^{\alpha_1}_{(n,\alpha_1)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha_1}a^{\alpha_n},$$
$f_2=f:H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta\rightarrow H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta$, $f(x\otimes y)=x_{(1,\alpha)}\otimes (x_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha y)$ and recursively $f_n=g_n(id\otimes f_{n-1})$. Since $f$ is invertible with $f^{-1}(x\otimes y)=x_{(1,\alpha)}\otimes (T_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}y)$ and the $g_n$ are invertible, it follows that the $g_n$ are invertible by induction.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $(H, K,\leftharpoonup,\rightharpoonup)$ be a matched pair of Hopf group algebra and $\pi=\pi_1\bigoplus\pi_2$, then $K\otimes H=\{(K\otimes H)_{(\gamma,\alpha)}=K_\gamma\otimes H_\alpha\}_{(\gamma,\alpha)\in\pi}$ becomes a Hopf $\pi$-algebra with the following structures:
\begin{align*}
&(a\otimes x)(b\otimes y)=a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})\otimes(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y,\\
&(a\otimes x)_{(1,(\gamma,\alpha))}\otimes (a\otimes x)_{(2,(\gamma,\alpha))}=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\otimes x_{(1,\gamma)})\otimes (a_{(2,\alpha)}\otimes x_{(2,\gamma)}),\\
&\varepsilon_{(\gamma,\alpha)}(a\otimes x)=\varepsilon_{K,\gamma}(a) \varepsilon_{H,\alpha}(x),\\
&S_{(\gamma,\alpha)}(a\otimes x)=(S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(2,\gamma)}))\otimes(S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)})),
\end{align*}
for all $x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta,a\in K_\gamma,b\in K_\delta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For all $x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta,z\in H_\mu,a\in K_\gamma,b\in K_\delta,c\in K_\nu$,
\begin{align*}
&[(a\otimes x)(b\otimes y)](c\otimes z)\\
&=[a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})\otimes(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y](c\otimes z)\\
&=a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})[((x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y)_{(1,\alpha\beta)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta}c_{(1,\nu)}]\\
&\quad\otimes[((x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y)_{(2,\alpha\beta)}\leftharpoonup_{\nu}c_{(2,\nu)}]z\\
                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                        
&=a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})[(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y_{(1,\beta)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta}c_{(1,\nu)}]\\
&\quad\otimes[(x_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(3,\delta)})y_{(2,\beta)}\leftharpoonup_{\nu}c_{(2,\nu)}]z\\
&=a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})[(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}(y_{(1,\beta)}\rightharpoonup_{\beta}c_{(1,\nu)})]\\
&\quad\otimes[((x_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(3,\beta)})\leftharpoonup_\nu (y_{(2,\beta)}\rightharpoonup_{\beta}c_{(2,\nu)}))(y_{(3,\beta)}\leftharpoonup_{\nu}c_{(3,\nu)})]z\\
&=a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha} b_{(1,\delta)}(y_{(1,\beta)}\rightharpoonup_{\beta}c_{(1,\nu)}))\\
&\quad\otimes[(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_{\delta\nu} b_{(2,\delta)} (y_{(2,\beta)}\rightharpoonup_{\beta}c_{(2,\nu)}))(y_{(2,\beta)}\leftharpoonup_{\nu}c_{(2,\nu)})]z\\
&=(a\otimes x)(b(y_{(1,\beta)}\rightharpoonup_\beta c_{(1,\nu)})\otimes(y_{(2,\beta)}\leftharpoonup_\nu c_{(2,\nu)})z)\\
&=(a\otimes x)[(b\otimes y)(c\otimes z)],
\end{align*}
thus $K\otimes H$ is associative. 
\begin{align*}
&\Delta_{(\gamma\delta,\alpha\beta)}((a\otimes x)(b\otimes y))\\
&=\Delta_{(\gamma\delta,\alpha\beta)}(a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})\otimes(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y)\\
&=(a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)}))_{(1,\gamma\delta)}\otimes((x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y)_{(1,\alpha\beta)}\\
&\quad \otimes(a(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)}))_{(2,\gamma\delta)}\otimes((x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})y)_{(2,\alpha\beta)}\\
&=a_{(1,\gamma)}(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})_{(1,\delta)}\otimes(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})_{(1,\alpha)}y_{(1,\beta)}\\
&\quad \otimes a_{(2,\gamma)}(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})_{(2,\delta)}\otimes(x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(2,\delta)})_{(2,\alpha)}y_{(2,\beta)}\\
&=a_{(1,\gamma)}(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})\otimes(x_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(3,\beta)})y_{(1,\beta)}\\
&\quad \otimes a_{(2,\gamma)}(x_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(2,\delta)})\otimes(x_{(4,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(4,\beta)})y_{(2,\beta)}\\
&=a_{(1,\gamma)}(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\delta)})\otimes (x_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(2,\delta)})y_{(1,\beta)}\\
&\quad \otimes a_{(2,\gamma)}(x_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(3,\delta)})\otimes(x_{(4,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\delta b_{(4,\delta)})y_{(2,\beta)}\\
&=\Delta_{(\gamma,\alpha)}(a\otimes x)\Delta_{(\delta,\beta)}(b\otimes y),
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
&S_{(\gamma,\alpha)}(a_{(1,\gamma)}\otimes x_{(1,\alpha)})(a_{(2,\gamma)}\otimes x_{(2,\alpha)})\\
&=(S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(2,\gamma)})\otimes S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)}))(a_{(3,\gamma)}\otimes x_{(3,\alpha)})\\
&=(S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(2,\gamma)}))((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)}))_{(1,\bar{\alpha})}\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}} a_{(3,\gamma)})\\
&\quad\otimes((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)}))_{(2,\bar{\alpha})}\leftharpoonup_{\alpha} a_{(4,\gamma)})x_{(3,\alpha)}\\
&=(S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(2,\gamma)}))((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})_{(1,\bar{\alpha})}\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)})_{(1,\bar{\alpha})})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha} a_{(3,\gamma)})\\
&\quad\otimes((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})_{(2,\bar{\alpha})}\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)})_{(2,\bar{\alpha})})\leftharpoonup_{\alpha} a_{(4,\gamma)})x_{(3,\alpha)}\\
&=(S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(3,\gamma)}))((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(2,\gamma)}))\rightharpoonup_{\alpha} a_{(4,\gamma)})\\
&\quad\otimes((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)}))\leftharpoonup_{\alpha} a_{(5,\alpha)})x_{(4,\alpha)}\\
&=S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}(S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(3,\gamma)})a_{(4,\gamma)})\otimes((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)}))\leftharpoonup_{\alpha} a_{(5,\alpha)})x_{(3,\alpha)}\\
&=((S_{H,\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)})\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\gamma}}S_{K,\gamma}(a_{(1,\gamma)})a_{(2,\gamma)})x_{(2,\alpha)}\\
&=\varepsilon_{K,\alpha}(a) \varepsilon_{H,\alpha}(x).
\end{align*}
Similarly $(a_{(1,\gamma)}\otimes x_{(1,\alpha)})S_{\gamma,\alpha}(a_{(2,\gamma)}\otimes x_{(2,\alpha)})=\varepsilon_{K,\gamma}(a) \varepsilon_{H,\alpha}(x).$

label: pro:brace
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro:brace}
Let $\pi$ be an abelian group and  $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ be a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-brace, then $(H_\circ,H_\circ)$ is a matched pair of cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-braces with 
$$x\rightharpoonup_\alpha a=S_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)})(x_{(2,\alpha)}\circ a),\ x\leftharpoonup_\beta a=T_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\beta a_{(1,\beta)})\circ x_{(2,\alpha)}\circ a_{(2,\beta)},$$
for all $x\in H_\alpha,a\in H_\beta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For all $x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta,a\in H_\gamma,b\in H_\delta$,
\begin{align*}
&(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})\circ((x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_{\gamma}a_{(2,\gamma)})\rightharpoonup_\alpha b))\\
&=(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})_{(1,\gamma)}((x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})_{(2,\gamma)}\rightharpoonup_\gamma((x_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_{\gamma}a_{(2,\gamma)})\rightharpoonup_\alpha b))\\
&=(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})(((x_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(2,\gamma)})\circ(x_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(3,\gamma)}))\rightharpoonup_{\gamma\alpha} b)\\
&=(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})((x_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\gamma}a_{(2,\gamma)})\circ T_\gamma(x_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\gamma a_{(3,\gamma)})\circ x_{(4,\alpha)}\circ a_{(4,\gamma)})\rightharpoonup_{\gamma\alpha} b)\\
&=(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})( (x_{(2,\alpha)}\circ a_{(2,\gamma)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\gamma} b)\\
&=(x_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}a_{(1,\gamma)})(x_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha (a_{(2,\gamma)}\rightharpoonup_\gamma b))\\
&=x\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}( a_{(1,\gamma)}(a_{(2,\gamma)}\rightharpoonup_\gamma b))\\
&=x\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}(a\circ b),
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
&(a\leftharpoonup_\gamma(b_{(1,\delta)}\rightharpoonup_\delta x_{(1,\alpha)}))\circ(b_{(2,\delta)}\leftharpoonup_\alpha x_{(2,\alpha)}))\\
&=T_\alpha(a_{(1,\gamma)}\circ b_{(1,\delta)}\rightharpoonup_{\gamma\delta} x_{(1,\alpha)})\circ a_{(2,\beta)}\circ(b_{(2,\delta)}\rightharpoonup_\delta x_{(2,\alpha)})\circ T_\alpha(b_{(3,\delta)}\rightharpoonup_\delta x_{(3,\alpha)})\circ b_{(4,\delta)}\circ x_{(4,\alpha)}\\
&=T_\alpha(a_{(1,\gamma)}\circ b_{(1,\delta)}\rightharpoonup_{\gamma\delta} x_{(1,\alpha)})\circ a_{(2,\beta)}\circ b_{(2,\delta)}\circ x_{(2,\alpha)}\\
&=(a\circ b)\leftharpoonup_\alpha x.
\end{align*}

label: pro:mp
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For all $a\in H_\alpha,b\in H_\beta,c\in H_\gamma$,
\begin{align*}
\Delta_{\alpha\beta}(ab)&=\Delta_{\alpha\beta}(a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b))\\
&=\Delta_\alpha(a)\circ\Delta_\beta(T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b)\\
&=\Delta_\alpha(a)\Delta_\beta(b),
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
a_{(1,\alpha)}(a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}b)&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}(a_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_{\alpha}b))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ((T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\circ a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{e}b))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(1\circ b)\\
&=a\circ b.
\end{align*}
Since
\begin{align*}
&a\rightharpoonup_\alpha(bc)=a\rightharpoonup_\alpha(b_{(1,\beta)}\circ(T_\beta(b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}}c))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\beta)})\circ((a_{(2,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_\alpha(T_\beta(b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}}c))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\beta)})((a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_\beta((a_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(3,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_\alpha(T_\beta(b_{(4,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}}c)))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\beta)})((a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(2,\beta)})\circ(a_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(3,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta}(T_\beta(b_{(4,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}}c)))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\beta)})((a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\alpha\beta}(T_\beta(b_{(4,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}}c))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b_{(1,\beta)})(a_{(2,\alpha)} \rightharpoonup_{\alpha}(b_{(2,\beta)}T_\beta(b_{(4,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{e}c))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha b)(a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha c).
\end{align*}
we have
\begin{align*}
a(bc)&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}(bc))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ((T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b_{(1,\beta)})(T_\alpha(a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}c))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b_{(1,\beta)})\circ (T_\beta(T_\alpha(a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}}(T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}c))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}b_{(1,\beta)})\circ(T_\beta(T_\alpha(a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b_{(2,\beta)})\circ T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}\bar{\beta}}c)\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}b_{(1,\beta)})\circ(T_{\alpha\beta}(a_{(4,\alpha)}\circ (T_\alpha(a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}b_{(2,\beta)})) \rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}\bar{\beta}}c)\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}b_{(1,\beta)})\circ(T_{\alpha\beta}(a_{(3,\alpha)}b_{(2,\beta)}) \rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}\bar{\beta}}c)\\
&=(ab)c.
\end{align*}
For the antipode $S$,
\begin{align*}
a_{(1,\alpha)}S_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})&=a_{(1,\alpha)}(a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha T_\alpha(a_{(3,\alpha)}))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ(T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}(a_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)})))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ((T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\circ a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_\eta T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)}))\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})\\
&=\varepsilon_\alpha(a)1,
\end{align*}
and using (\ref{mp6}) we have
$$T_\beta(a\rightharpoonup_\alpha b)=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_\beta b_{(1,\beta)})\circ T_{\alpha\beta}(a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ b_{(2,\beta)}).$$
Thus
\begin{align*}
&S_\alpha(a_{(1,\alpha)})a_{(2,\alpha)}\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)}))\circ(T_{\bar{\alpha}}(a_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)}))\rightharpoonup_\alpha a_{(5,\alpha)})\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)}))\circ((a_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)}))\circ T_{e}(a_{(5,\alpha)}\circ T_\alpha(a_{(6,\alpha)}))\rightharpoonup_\alpha a_{(7,\alpha)})\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)}))\circ((a_{(3,\alpha)}\leftharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha(a_{(4,\alpha)}))\rightharpoonup_\alpha a_{(5,\alpha)})\\
&=a_{(1,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha( T_\alpha(a_{(2,\alpha)})a_{(3,\alpha)})\\
&=\varepsilon_\alpha(a)1.
\end{align*}
For the compatibility condition, we have
\begin{align*}
&(a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ b)S(a_{(2,\alpha)})(a_{(3,\alpha)}\circ c)\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ b)S(a_{(2,\alpha)})a_{(3,\alpha)}(a_{(4,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha c)\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ b)(a_{(2,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha c)\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ b_{(1,\beta)})\circ(T_{\alpha\beta}(a_{(2,\alpha)}\circ b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\alpha}\bar{\beta}}(a_{(3,\alpha)}\rightharpoonup_\alpha c))\\
&=(a_{(1,\alpha)}\circ b_{(1,\beta)})\circ((T_{\beta}(b_{(2,\beta)})\circ T_{\alpha}(a_{(2,\alpha)})\circ a_{(3,\alpha)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}} c)\\
&=a\circ (b_{(1,\beta)}\circ(T_{\beta}(b_{(2,\beta)})\rightharpoonup_{\bar{\beta}} c))\\
&=a\circ (b_{(1,\beta)}\circ(bc).
\end{align*}
The proof is completed.

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $\pi$ be an abelian group and $(H,\cdot,1,\Delta,\varepsilon,S)$ a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra. The category $\mathbf{Br}(H)$ and $\mathbf{M_p}(H)$ are equivalent.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Define $F:\mathbf{Br}(H)\rightarrow \mathbf{M_p}(H)$ by $F((H,\cdot,\circ))=(H_\circ,H_\circ)$, where the matched pair $(H_\circ,H_\circ)$ is given in Proposition \ref{pro:brace}. For any morphism in $\mathbf{Br}(H)$, $F(f)=f$. Clearly $F$ is a functor.

Conversely define $G:\mathbf{M_p}(H)\rightarrow\mathbf{Br}(H)$ by $F(H,H)=(H,\cdot,\circ)$, where $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ is the Hopf brace given in Proposition \ref{pro:mp}, and $G(f)=f$ for any morphism in $\mathbf{M_p}(H)$. It is easy to see that $G$ is a functor. By an routine exercise, $\mathbf{Br}(H)$ and $\mathbf{M_p}(H)$ are equivalent.

label: eq:P3
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\triangleright$ is a coalgebra homomorphism, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
x\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1 &=& (x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1) \varepsilon(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)\\
 &=& (x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)\cdot S_e(x_{(3,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)\\
 &\stackrel{\ref{eq:P1}}{=}& (x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)\cdot S(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)\\
 &=& \varepsilon_e(x\triangleright_{\alpha,e} 1)1 =\varepsilon_e(x)1.
\end{eqnarray*}

By Eq.~\eqref{eq:P-con},  we have
$\psi_{e,\alpha,1}\theta_{e,\alpha,1}=\theta_{e,\alpha,1}\psi_{e,\alpha,1}=id_{H_\alpha},$
which means that $\theta_{e,\alpha,1}$ is a linear automorphism of $H_\alpha$. On the other hand, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\theta_{e,\alpha,1}^2(x) = 1\triangleright_{e,\alpha} (1\triangleright_{e,\alpha} x)
\stackrel{\eqref{eq:P2}}{=}  (1\triangleright_{e,\alpha} 1)\triangleright_{e,\alpha} (x)
\stackrel{\eqref{eq:P3}}{=}  1\triangleright_{e,\alpha} x = \theta_{e,\alpha,1}(x).
\end{eqnarray*}
Hence, $1\triangleright_{e,\alpha} (x) = \theta_{e,\alpha,1}(x) = x$.
Finally we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
S_\beta(x\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y)&=&S_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\varepsilon_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})\varepsilon_\beta(y_{(2,\beta)}) \\
 &\stackrel{\ref{eq:P3}}{=}& S_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\cdot(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} \varepsilon_\beta(y_{(2,\beta)})1)\\
&=&S_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\cdot(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} (y_{(2,\beta)}\cdot S_\beta(y_3))) \\
 &\stackrel{\ref{eq:P1}}{=}& S_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\cdot(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)})\cdot(x_{(3,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha}} S_\beta(y_{(3,\beta)}))\\
&=&\varepsilon_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} S_\beta(y_{(2,\beta)}))\\
&=&\varepsilon_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)})\varepsilon_\beta(y_{(1,\beta)})(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright S_\beta(y_{(2,\beta)}))=x\triangleright S_\beta(y). 
\end{eqnarray*}
These finish the proof.

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\triangleright$ is a coalgebra homomorphism and $H$ is cocommutative, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\Delta_{\alpha,\beta}(x *_{\alpha,\beta} y)&=&\Delta_{\alpha,\beta}(x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\beta)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y))\\
&=&\Delta_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)})\cdot \Delta_{\alpha,\beta}(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y)\\
&=&(x_{(1,\alpha)}\otimes x_{(2,\alpha)})\cdot((x_{(3,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\otimes(x_{(4,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)}))\\
&=&(x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(3,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)}))\otimes (x_{(2,\alpha)}\cdot(x_{(4,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)}))\\
&=&(x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)}))\otimes (x_{(3,\alpha)}\cdot(x_{(4,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)}))\\
&=&(x_{(1,\alpha)} *_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\otimes(x_{(2,\alpha)} *_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)})
                                        
\end{eqnarray*}
for all $x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta, \alpha,\beta\in\pi$, which implies  that the comultiplication $\Delta$ is an algebra homomorphism with respect to the multiplication $*_{\alpha,\beta}$. 
Moreover, we have
\begin{align*}
  \varepsilon_\beta(x *_{\alpha,\beta} y) & =\varepsilon_\beta(x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y)) \\
  & =\varepsilon_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)})\varepsilon_\beta(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y)=\varepsilon_\alpha(x)\varepsilon_\beta(y),
\end{align*}
which implies  that the counit $\varepsilon$ is also an algebra homomorphism with respect to the multiplication $*_{\alpha,\beta}$. 
Since the comultiplication $\Delta$ is an algebra homomorphism with respect to the multiplication $\cdot$, 
for all $x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta,z\in H_\gamma, \alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\pi$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
(x *_{\alpha,\beta} y)*_{\alpha\beta,\gamma} z&=& (x_{(1,\alpha)} *_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\cdot((x_{(2,\alpha)} *_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)})\triangleright_{\alpha\beta,\gamma} z)\\
&=&(x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)}))\cdot((x_{(3,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(4,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(2,\beta)}))\triangleright_{\alpha\beta,\gamma} z)\\
&\stackrel{\eqref{eq:P2}}{=}&x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y_{(1,\beta)})\cdot (x_{(3,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\gamma} (y_{(2,\beta)}\triangleright_{\beta,\gamma} z))\\
&\stackrel{\eqref{eq:P1}}{=}&x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} (y_{(1,\beta)}\cdot (y_{(2,\beta)}\triangleright_{\beta,\gamma} z)))\\
&=&x *_{\alpha,\beta\gamma} (y*_{\beta,\gamma} z),
\end{eqnarray*}
which implies that the multiplication $*_{\alpha,\beta}$ is associative.  
For any $x\in H_\alpha, \alpha\in\pi$, by  \eqref{eq:P3} and \eqref{eq:P4}, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
x *_{\alpha,e} 1&=&x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} 1)=x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot\varepsilon_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})=x,\\
1 *_{e,\alpha} x&=&1\cdot (1\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} x)=x.
\end{eqnarray*}
Since $\triangleright$ is a coalgebra homomorphism and $H$ is cocommutative, we know that
$$\Delta_\beta\psi_{\alpha,\beta,x}=(\psi_{\alpha,\beta,x_{(1,\alpha)}}\otimes\psi_{\alpha,\beta,x_{(2,\alpha)}})\Delta_\beta,$$
and $T$ is a coalgebra homomorphism. Also, note that
\begin{eqnarray*}
x_{(1,\alpha)}*_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha}} T_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)}) 
&\stackrel{\ref{post-rbb-1}}{=}& x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha}} T_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)}))\\
&\stackrel{\ref{post-rbb-2}}{=}& x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot(\theta_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha},x_{(2,\alpha)}}(\psi_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha},x_{(3,\alpha)}}(S_\alpha(x_{(4,\alpha)}))))\\
&=& x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot(\varepsilon_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})S_\alpha(x_{(3,\alpha)}))\\
&=& \varepsilon_\alpha(x)1,
\end{eqnarray*}
and this implies that
\begin{eqnarray*}
T_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha(x) &=& \varepsilon_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)})T_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)}) \\
&=& (x_{(1,\alpha)}*_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha}} T_{\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)}))*_{e,\alpha} T_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha(x_{(3,\alpha)})\\
&=& x_{(1,\alpha)}*_{\alpha,e} (T_{\alpha}(x_{(2,\alpha)})*_{\bar{\alpha},\alpha} T_{\bar{\alpha}}(T_\alpha(x_{(3,\alpha)})))\\
&=& x_{(1,\alpha)}*_{\alpha,e} \varepsilon_{\bar{\alpha}}(T_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)}))1 = x,
\end{eqnarray*}
and
\begin{eqnarray*}
T_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)}) *_{\bar{\alpha},\alpha} x_{(2,\alpha)} &=&  T_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)}) *_{\bar{\alpha},\alpha} T_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})\\
 &=& \varepsilon_{\bar{\alpha}}(T_\alpha(x))1 = \varepsilon_\alpha(x)1.
\end{eqnarray*}
Therefore, $(H,*,1,\Delta,\varepsilon,T)$ is a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra.

Moreover, we have
$$ (x *_{\alpha,\beta} y)\triangleright_{\alpha\beta,\gamma} z=(x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y))\triangleright_{\alpha\beta,\gamma} z=x\triangleright_{\alpha,\gamma} (y\triangleright_{\beta,\gamma} z). $$
Then by (\ref{eq:P1}) and (\ref{eq:P3}), $(H_e ,\cdot,1)$ is a left $\pi$-$H_\triangleright$-modulelike. 
Since $\triangleright_{(\alpha,\beta)}$ is also a coalgebra homomorphism, $(H_e,\cdot,1,\Delta_e,\varepsilon_e,S_e)$ is a left $\pi$-$H_\triangleright$-modulelike $\pi$-bialgebra via the action $\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta}$.

label: thm:br
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:br}
Let $(H,\triangleright)$ be a cocommutative post-Hopf $\pi$-algebra. Then $(H,\cdot,1,\Delta,\varepsilon,S)$  and  the subadjacent Hopf $\pi$-algebra $(H,*,1,\Delta,\varepsilon,T)$ form a Hopf $\pi$-brace. 
Conversely, any cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-brace $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ gives a post-Hopf $\pi$-algebra  $(H,\triangleright)$ with $\triangleright$ defined by 
$$x\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y=S_\alpha(x_{(1,\alpha)})\cdot_{\bar{\alpha},\beta}(x_{(2,\alpha)}\circ_{\alpha,\beta} y), \quad \forall x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta, \alpha,\beta\in\pi.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(H,\triangleright)$ be a cocommutative post-Hopf $\pi$-algebra. We only need to show that the multiplications $\cdot$ and $*$ satisfy the compatibility  condition (\ref{eq:Hbrace}), which follows from
\begin{align*}
x*_{\alpha,\beta}(y\cdot z)&=x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot (x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta\gamma}(y\cdot z))\\
&=x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot((x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y)\cdot (x_{(3,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\gamma} z))\\
&=x_{(1,\alpha)}\cdot(x_{(2,\alpha)}\triangleright_{\alpha,\beta} y)\cdot S_\alpha(x_{(3,\alpha)})\cdot x_{(4,\alpha)}\cdot (x_5\triangleright_{\alpha,\gamma} z)\\
&=(x_{(1,\alpha)}*_{\alpha,\beta} y)\cdot S_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})\cdot (x_{(3,\alpha)}*_{\alpha,\beta} z),
\end{align*}
for any $x\in H_\alpha,y\in H_\beta,z\in H_\gamma, \alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\pi$.

Conversely, it is straightforward but tedious to check that a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-brace $(H,\cdot,\circ)$ induces a post-Hopf $\pi$-algebra  $(H,\triangleright)$.

\begin{enumerate}[\rm(1)]
  \item When the group $\pi=\{1\}$, we could recover the notion of Rota-Baxter Hopf algebras.
  \item It is obvious that the antipode $S$ is a Rota-Baxter operator on $H$.
  \item Let $(H,B)$ be a Rota-Baxter Hopf $\pi$-algebra, and $\varphi$ a $\pi$-bialgebra automorphism or antiautomorphism of $H$. Then $B^{(\varphi)}=\{B^{(\varphi)}_\alpha=\varphi_{\bar{\alpha}}\circ B_\alpha\circ\varphi^{-1}_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ is also a  Rota-Baxter operator on $H$.

title: Example
body_md:
Let $(H,\Delta,\varepsilon,S,B)$ be a Rota-Baxter Hopf algebra and $\pi=Aut(H)$ the group of Hopf algebras automorphisms of $H$. For each $\alpha\in\pi$, $H_\alpha=H$ as a vector space. We denote the element in $H_\alpha$ by $h^\alpha=\alpha(h)$ for $h\in H$. Define
\begin{align*}
&m_{\alpha,\beta}:H_\alpha\otimes H_\beta\rightarrow H_{\alpha\beta},\ g^\alpha\otimes h^\beta\mapsto (gh)^{\alpha\beta},\\
&\Delta_\alpha=\Delta,\quad \varepsilon_\alpha=\varepsilon,\\
&S_\alpha:H_\alpha\rightarrow H_{\bar{\alpha}},\ h^\alpha\mapsto S(h)^{\bar{\alpha}},\\
&B_\alpha:H_\alpha\rightarrow H_{\bar{\alpha}},\ h^\alpha\mapsto B(h)^{\bar{\alpha}},
\end{align*}
then $(\{H_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in \pi},\{B_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in \pi})$ is a Rota-Baxter Hopf $\pi$-algebra.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $H=\{H_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ be a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra. Suppose that $G_\alpha$ is a Hopf subalgebra of $H_e$ and $K_\alpha$ is a subcoalgebra of $H_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in\pi$, such that $G=\{G_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ is a Hopf $\pi$-algebra and $K=\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ is a Hopf $\pi$-subalgebra of $H_\alpha$, and as a Hopf $\pi$-algebra $H=GK$, i.e., $H_\alpha=G_\alpha K_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in\pi$. 
Suppose that the product is direct, that is, $H$ is isomorphic to $G\otimes K=\{G_\alpha \otimes K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ as a family of vector spaces. Define a family of maps $B=\{B_\alpha:H_\alpha\rightarrow H_{\bar{\alpha}}\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ by
$$B_\alpha (h h')=\varepsilon_e(h)S_\alpha(h'),$$
where $h_1\in G_\alpha, h_2\in K_\alpha$. 
Then $B$ is a Rota-Baxter operator of $H$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Clearly, $B$ is a family of well-defined linear maps. 
First we prove that each $B_\alpha$ is a coalgebra map. For $x=hg\in H_\alpha$, where $h\in G_\alpha$, $g\in K_\alpha$ we have:
\begin{eqnarray*}
\Delta_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(x))&=&\varepsilon_e(h)\Delta_{\bar{\alpha}}(S_\alpha(g))=\varepsilon_e(h) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(g_{(2,\alpha)})\otimes S_{\bar{\alpha}}(g_{(1,\alpha)})\\
&=&\varepsilon_e(h_{(1,e)})S_{\bar{\alpha}}(g_{(1,\alpha)})\otimes \varepsilon_e(h_{(2,e)})S_{\bar{\alpha}}(g_{(2,\alpha)})\\
&=&(B_{\bar{\alpha}}\otimes B_{\bar{\alpha}})\Delta_\alpha(x).
\end{eqnarray*}

In order to prove that $B$ satisfies (\ref{eq:RBO}) consider $x=hg\in H_\alpha$  and $y=h'g'\in H_\beta$, where $h\in G_\alpha, g\in K_\alpha$, $h'\in G_\beta, g'\in K_\beta$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\pi$. We have
\begin{eqnarray*}
 &&B_{\beta\alpha}(x_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(x_{(2,\alpha)})yS_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(x_{(3,\alpha)})))\\
 &=&B_{\beta\alpha}((h_{(1,e)}g_{(1,\alpha)})(\varepsilon_e(h_{(2,e)})S_\alpha (g_{(2,\alpha)}))(h'g')(\varepsilon_e(h_{(3,e)})S_{\bar{\alpha}}(S_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}))))\\
 &=&B_{\beta\alpha}(\varepsilon_e(h_{(1,e)})\varepsilon_e(h_{(2,e)})h_{(3,e)}g_{(1,\alpha)}S_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)}) h'g' g_{(3,\alpha)})\\
 &=&B_{\beta\alpha}(hh' g' \varepsilon_e(g_{(1,\alpha)})g_{(2,\alpha)}) = B_{\beta\alpha}(hh'g'g)\\
 &=&\varepsilon_{e}(hh')S_{\beta\alpha}(g'g)=\varepsilon_e(h)\varepsilon_e(h')S_\alpha(g)S_\beta(g')\\
 &=&B_\alpha(x)B_\beta(y).
\end{eqnarray*}

Since $H_\alpha=G_\alpha K_\alpha$ is spanned by elements of the form $hg$, where $h\in G_\alpha$, $g\in K_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in\pi$, the equation (\ref{eq:RBO}) holds for all $x,y\in H$.

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) First, we prove $m=\{m_{\alpha,\beta}\}_{\alpha,\beta\in\pi}$ is  associative. For all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta, \ell\in H_\gamma, ~\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\pi$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
                                                      
& & (g\circ_B h) \circ_B\ell \\
&=& (g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})hS_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}))) \circ_B\ell \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})h_{(1,\beta)}S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}))  B_{\beta\alpha}\big( g_{(4,\alpha)} B_\alpha(g_{(5,\alpha)})h_{(2,\beta)}S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(6,\alpha)})) \big) \\
&&\quad \ell S_{\bar{\beta\alpha}}\big(B_{\beta\alpha}( g_{(7,\alpha)} B_\alpha(g_{(8,\alpha)})h_{(3,\beta)}S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(9,\alpha)})) )\big) \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})h_{(1,\beta)}S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}))  B_\alpha(g_{(4,\alpha)})   B_\beta(h_{(2,\beta)})\ell  S_{\bar{\beta\alpha}}( B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}) B_\beta(h_{(3,\beta)}) ) \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})h_{(1,\beta)} B_\beta(h_{(2,\beta)})\ell S_{\bar{\beta}}(B_\beta(h_{(3,\beta)})) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})) \\
&=& g\circ_B( h_{(1,\beta)} B_\beta(h_{(2,\beta)})\ell S_{\bar{\beta}}(B_\beta(h_{(3,\beta)})) ) \\
&=& g\circ_B(h\circ_B \ell).
\end{eqnarray*}



  Then, we prove $m=\{m_{\alpha,\beta}\}_{\alpha,\beta\in\pi}$ is a $\pi$-coalgebra homomorphism. For all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta, ~\alpha,\beta\in\pi$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & (g\circ_B h)_{(1,\alpha\beta)} \otimes (g\circ_B h)_{(2,\alpha\beta)} = (g\circ_B h)_{(1,\beta\alpha)} \otimes (g\circ_B h)_{(2,\beta\alpha)} \\
&=& (g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})hS_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})))_{(1,\beta\alpha)} \otimes (g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})hS_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})))_{(2,\beta\alpha)}  \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})h_{(1,\beta)}S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})) \otimes g_{(4,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(5,\alpha)})h_{(2,\beta)}S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(6,\alpha)}))  \\
&=& (g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ_B h_{(1,\beta)})\otimes(g_{(2,\alpha)}\circ_B h_{(2,\beta)}).
\end{eqnarray*}

  Last, we prove $T=\{T_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ is an antipode. For all $h\in H_\alpha, ~\alpha\in\pi$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & m_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha}}(id_{H_{\alpha}} \otimes T_\alpha)\Delta_\alpha(h) \\
&=& h_{(1,\alpha)} \circ_B S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}))S_\alpha(h_{(3,\alpha)})B_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)}) \\
&=& h_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(3,\alpha)}))S_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)})B_\alpha(h_{(5,\alpha)}) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(6,\alpha)})) \\
&=& h_{(1,\alpha)} \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}) S_\alpha(h_{(3,\alpha)}) \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)}) 1_e \\
&=& \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(1,\alpha)}) \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}) 1_e \\
&=& \varepsilon_\alpha(h)1_e.
\end{eqnarray*}

So $m_{\alpha,\bar{\alpha}}(id_{H_{\alpha}} \otimes T_\alpha)\Delta_\alpha = \varepsilon_\alpha 1_e$. Similarly prove $m_{\bar{\alpha},\alpha}(T_\alpha \otimes id_{H_{\alpha}})\Delta_\alpha = \varepsilon_\alpha 1_e$. 
Hence, $H$ with the new multiplication $m=\{m_{\alpha,\beta}\}_{\alpha\in\pi}$ and antipode $T=\{T_{\alpha,\beta}\}_{\alpha\in\pi})$  is a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra

(2) For all $h\in H_\alpha, ~\alpha\in\pi$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & B_\alpha(h_{(1,\alpha)})B_{\bar{\alpha}}(T_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)})) \\
&=& B_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)}) B_{\bar{\alpha}}(S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}))S_\alpha(h_{(3,\alpha)})B_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)}))  \\
&=& B_e(h_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(3,\alpha)}))S_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)})B_\alpha(h_{(5,\alpha)}) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(6,\alpha)}))) \\
&=& B_e(h_{(1,\alpha)} \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}) S_\alpha(h_{(3,\alpha)}) \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(4,\alpha)}) 1_e) \\
&=& \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(1,\alpha)}) \varepsilon_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}) B_e(1_e) \\
&=& \varepsilon_\alpha(h)1_e.
\end{eqnarray*}

From the above and $B_\alpha(h_{(1,\alpha)})S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(h_{(2,\alpha)}))=\varepsilon_\alpha(B_\alpha(h))=\varepsilon_\alpha(x)1_e$, we have $B_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha$ and $S_{\bar{\alpha}}B_\alpha$ are the convolutional inverse for $B_\alpha$. Hence $B_{\bar{\alpha}}T_\alpha = S_{\bar{\alpha}}B_\alpha$, for all $\alpha\in\pi$.

(3) From Eq. (\ref{eq:RBO}) and (\ref{eq:RBHm}), we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
 B_{\alpha\beta}(g \circ_B h) &=& B_{\beta\alpha}(g \circ_B h) \\
 &=& B_{\beta\alpha}( g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})h S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})) ) \\
 &=& B_\alpha(g) B_\beta(h),
\end{eqnarray*}
for all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta, ~\alpha,\beta\in\pi$.

Then we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & B_{\beta\alpha}\big(g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ_B B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})\circ_B h \circ_B T_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}))\big) \\
&=& B_{\alpha}(g_{(1,\alpha)}) B_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})) B_{\beta}(h) B_{\alpha}(T_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)}))) \\
&=& B_{\alpha}(g_{(1,\alpha)}) B_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})) B_{\beta}(h) S_{\alpha}(B_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})))  \\
&=& B_{\alpha}(g) \circ_B B_{\alpha}(h).
\end{eqnarray*}
for all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta, ~\alpha,\beta\in\pi$. The operator $B$ is also a Rota-Baxter operator on the cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra $H_B$.

(4) From (3), it is evident that the family of maps $B:H_B\rightarrow H$ is a homomorphism of Rota-Baxter Hopf $\pi$-algebras.

By Lemma \ref{lem:nH}, $(H,\circ_B,T)$ is a cocommutative Hopf $\pi$-algebra. For all $g\in H_\alpha, h\in H_\beta, \ell\in H_\gamma, ~\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\pi$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & (g_{(1,\alpha)}\circ_B h)S_{\bar{\alpha}}(g_{(2,\alpha)})(g_{(3,\alpha)}\circ_B \ell) \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})hS_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})) S_{\bar{\alpha}}(g_{(4,\alpha)}) g_{(5,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(6,\alpha)})\ell S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(7,\alpha)})) \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})hS_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})) B_\alpha(g_{(4,\alpha)})\ell S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(5,\alpha)})) \\
&=& g_{(1,\alpha)}B_\alpha(g_{(2,\alpha)})h\ell S_{\bar{\alpha}}(B_\alpha(g_{(3,\alpha)})) \\
&=& g\circ_B(h\ell).
\end{eqnarray*}
Hence $(H,\cdot,\circ_B)$ is a cocommutative $\pi$-Hopf brace.
